executiveSummary: OT/ICS risk is elevated this cycle due to concurrent, actively exploited edge vulnerabilities and multiple high-impact OT-native advisories. Mass exploitation of the PHP "php2shell" vulnerabilities (CVE-2026-109618/-109619) is disrupting public-facing services and enables web shell deployment; immediate patching and DMZ containment are essential. View Article Security Advisory Perimeter devices remain a primary ingress vector: NetScaler ADC/Gateway multi-CVEs are under active exploitation against VPN gateways; rapid patching and compromise assessment are required. Security Advisory OT-native exposure increased with critical flaws in industrial gateways and device managers: Advantech EKI-1242 series (unauthenticated device control, OPC UA DoS) and Danfoss iC7 drives (unsigned code/firmware upload paths) present risks of process manipulation or disruption if reachable. CISA Weekly CISA Weekly CISA warns of active reconnaissance and tooling against Siemens S7 PLCs over S7comm (TCP/102). Internet exposure or weak segmentation could enable read/write to controllers. Immediate removal from the internet, strong access protections, and S7 traffic monitoring are advised. Security Advisory Additional escalations: actively exploited BeyondTrust Remote Support (Bomgar) auth bypass on self-hosted appliances, widely used for vendor access and remote support, and SiteGuard Server Edition OS command injection used for full server compromise via a default feature. Security Advisory Security Advisory

relevance: The current threat picture combines high-velocity exploitation of web and VPN perimeters with credible, high-impact vulnerabilities in OT gateways, drives, and device managers. Even when CVEs originate in IT/web components (e.g., PHP), exposure of billing portals, vendor access UIs, or embedded web consoles in DMZs provides practical ingress to OT zones when segmentation or jump host controls are weak. Concurrently, ICS-native advisories (Advantech iGateway, Danfoss iC7, Siemens RUGGEDCOM) present direct manipulation paths that could affect control logic, firmware integrity, or process availability. CISA's S7 advisory confirms active reconnaissance/use of S7comm-reinforcing the need to remove direct internet reachability and monitor PLC protocol traffic at boundaries.

descriptions: Initial Access: Exploit Public-Facing Application (ATT&CK T1190), Valid Accounts (T1078) via VPN/MFA token replay
Execution: Web shell deployment post-PHP RCE; OS command injection on SiteGuard; remote command execution on appliances
Persistence/Privilege Escalation: Remote support appliance abuse, scheduled tasks/services, DLL sideloading (Lazarus)
Discovery/Lateral Movement: PsExec/WinRM/RDP (SafePay); traversal from DMZ perimeters to OT jump hosts; S7comm reads/writes on TCP/102
ICS-specific: S7comm PUT/GET writes; OPC UA session exhaustion; firmware/EEPROM manipulation on drives/gateways

outlook72h: Expect continued automated probing/exploitation of PHP and NetScaler perimeters; prioritize WAF tuning, log review, and rapid patch verification windows. Increase monitoring on remote-support and WAF appliances for anomalous admin actions; isolate if compromise indicators appear. Conduct targeted hunts on OT DMZs for unauthorized PLC protocol traffic (S7comm), unexpected firmware/config changes on gateways and drives. Prepare maintenance windows to update Envoy/Istio/Node stacks for Brotli fixes; consider temporary Brotli disablement on high-risk paths.
